verses.text: The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, because the band of men who came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the oldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.
Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.
He also walked in the ways of Ahab’s house, because his mother was his counselor in acting wickedly.
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, as did Ahab’s house, for they were his counselors after the death of his father, to his destruction.
He also followed their counsel, and went with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth Gilead, and the Syrians wounded Joram.

He returned to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which they had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.
Now the destruction of Ahaziah was of God, in that he went to Joram; for when he had come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom Yahweh had anointed to cut off Ahab’s house.
When Jehu was executing judgment on Ahab’s house, he found the princes of Judah and the sons of the brothers of Ahaziah, serving Ahaziah, and killed them.

He sought Ahaziah, and they caught him (now he was hiding in Samaria), and they brought him to Jehu, and killed him; and they buried him, for they said, “He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought Yahweh with all his heart.” The house of Ahaziah had no power to hold the kingdom.
Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring  of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, the king’s daughter, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stealthily rescued him from among the king’s sons who were slain, and put him and his nurse in the bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest (for she was the sister of Ahaziah), hid him from Athaliah, so that she didn’t kill him.
He was with them hidden in God’s house six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.

footnotes.content: The inhabitants of Jerusalem looked at a young man and saw a king. They didn't know yet that choosing the youngest—the one left standing after loss—would mean choosing a reign led by his mother's wicked heart. How often we settle for proximity to power when we should be asking: whose counsel does this leader follow?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Forty-two years old—an age when a man should have learned wisdom from long years of walking. But Ahaziah's mother, Athaliah, was the daughter of Omri, inheritor of a dynasty that had turned from the Lord. Age without right counsel is only age; it doesn't make us wise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A mother's hand on a son's shoulder can guide him toward the Lord or away from Him. Athaliah had no room in her heart for the God of Israel—only for the ways of Ahab's house, where Baal whispered and bloodshed was the language of power. He walked where she pointed, and that walking led him to ruin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After his father died, the counselors who surrounded Ahaziah were not righteous men but worshippers of Ahab's idols. They spoke wisdom only about war and earthly advantage, never about the Lord. We become what we listen to—and Ahaziah had closed his ears to any voice but theirs.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ramoth Gilead—a city contested in bloodshed, a place where foolish kings went to prove themselves in war. Ahaziah followed Jehoram of Israel into battle, not because God had called him there, but because wicked counsel had made such alliances seem necessary. The Syrians wounded Jehoram; the wound that mattered was already in Ahaziah's soul.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jezreel—the very city where Ahab and Jezebel had once ruled in wickedness and bloodshed. Ahaziah went there to be healed, not knowing he was stepping into the place where the Lord's judgment had already begun to fall. Sometimes the places we think will restore us are the ones that will destroy us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The text says plainly: 'The destruction of Ahaziah was of God.' This was not random—it was the Lord's judgment falling on a king who had spurned Him and chosen the counsels of the wicked. Jehu, though a rough instrument, had been anointed by the Lord to cut off Ahab's house, and Ahaziah walked straight into that judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The princes of Judah were found serving their king at the wrong place and in the wrong cause—standing with him against the Lord's anointed. Loyalty to a wicked king becomes our own ruin when that king has turned his face from God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even as Jehu struck him down, someone spoke Ahaziah's burial with a strange grace: 'He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart.' The memory of a righteous grandfather lingered, though the grandson had trampled it underfoot. It's a haunting mercy—even in death, the Lord was not finished with the house of Judah.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Athaliah's response to her son's death was not grief but ambition. She rose and destroyed the royal seed—not a mother's broken heart, but a tyrant's consolidation of power. When the wicked hold the throne, their first instinct is always to kill the next generation so no one can challenge them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehoshabeath—a king's daughter, a priest's wife, and a quiet rescuer—stole into the dark and saved one child from slaughter. While Athaliah hunted, this woman hid Joash in her own bedroom and later in the house of God. Sometimes the most faithful act is the one no one sees, done not for glory but for love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Six years in hiding—Joash lived in God's house while darkness reigned outside. Readers today hear an echo: there are seasons when the faithful must shelter in places of prayer, waiting for the Lord's deliverance. Even when judgment falls and wicked powers seem to have won, God's house holds safe those who belong to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
